Hero_Desc_Kyarot:
A sprite gardener who can make any crop grow big.
She has set up a garden around Yggdrasil and grows giant sugarcanes.
She used to disregard the Elves, who supply sugar, but maybe she's changed now?
Album_Like_Kyarot: Drinking coffee through a sugarcane straw, the towering trunk of Yggdrasil.
Album_Hate_Kyarot: A merchant selling rotten seeds, rusty scissors.
Album_Hobby_Kyarot: Creating a special nutrient formula with magic.
Album_Wish_Kyarot: Covering the Sprite Palace in ivy.
Album_Kyarot1: Kyarot's garden stands out even among the Sprite Kingdom. While most sprites rely on magical farming tools, Kyarot prefers to cultivate crops by hand. Plowing the soil and brewing fertilizers brings her pure joy. I always thought sprites would find farming tedious, but apparently not.
Album_Kyarot2: Kyarot has the magical ability to create a special kind of fertilizer. When used, plants grow so massive they border on monstrous. Kyarot is a mid-level Priestess of the Order, holding the special title of "First-Class Gardener." It seems the Order took notice of Kyarot's abilities because of this talent.
Album_Kyarot3: When I asked Kyarot what a First-Class Gardener actually does, she replied, "Not much, really. But with permission, I get to see Yggdrasil up close." Since Yggdrasil is the Sprite Kingdom's largest and most magnificent plant, Kyarot takes great pride in her title. But... wasn't Yggdrasil already open to visitors?
Album_Kyarot4: Kyarot grows coffee in her garden. Sugarcane and coffee? That's a strange mix, but this is Elias, after all... Most of the harvest goes to cafés, while the rest is brewed for personal use. I tried a cup, but it was so unbearably sweet. Kyarot drinks it through a sugarcane straw she grew herself—an extreme level of sweetness, even by sprite standards.
Album_Kyarot5: Kyarot's relationship with the elves is complicated. The elves look down on Kyarot for growing her own sugarcane, calling her a "primitive sugar-seeker." Meanwhile, Kyarot dismisses the elves as "factory-made sweet-seekers." Kyarot insists there is an unbridgeable chasm between these two forms of sugar... but to me, they both just taste sweet.
Album_Kyarot6: Kyarot is quite fond of Yggdrasil. But rather than seeing it as a religious symbol, she admires it from a horticultural perspective—as a beautifully grown plant. She often imagines pruning its branches or sprinkling it with her special fertilizer, but she refrains from doing so out of fear that Ner might ban her from the area. Isn't this technically sacrilege?
Album_Kyarot7: Kyarot is under Ner's watchful eye. Apparently, Kyarot once dumped a load of special fertilizer around the flower beds near Yggdrasil. While the tree itself was unaffected, the surrounding plants grew out of control, and it took a lot of effort to suppress them with magic. Ever since that incident, Kyarot was given an official position. Now, every time Kyarot asks for a permit to "manage" Yggdrasil, Ner struggles to come up with an excuse to refuse. At this point, doesn't that make Kyarot a special security concern?
